comparison: Perfect alignment on bioinformatics claims (C7, C63-C66). Both evaluations support the comprehensive bioinformatic analysis revealing conserved N-terminal motifs across bactofilin sequences. OpenEval provides detailed methodology while peer review emphasizes integration with other approaches.

Perfect alignment on client protein rescue claims (C11-C12, C75-C76). Both support findings that overproduced PbpC can restore membrane localization to MTS mutants but not polymerization mutants. Evidence described as solid and consistent by both.

Strong overlap on MTS mutagenesis and localization claims (C5, C30, C34-C37). Peer review R1 also includes membrane binding claims (C40-C45) that OpenEval separates into R4. Both describe evidence as solid with well-integrated experimental approaches.

Substantial overlap on membrane binding characterization (C38-C45). OpenEval R4 focuses on single-particle tracking, fractionation, and liposome binding. Peer review R1 groups these with mutagenesis data, emphasizing the comprehensive integration of techniques.

Strong alignment on domain swap experiments (C48-C52). OpenEval R6 also includes polymerization-membrane binding cooperativity claims (C8, C79-C80) that peer review addresses in R3. Both support the functional complementation approach.

Partial overlap on polymerization-membrane binding cooperativity (C8, C79-C80). OpenEval R6 includes domain swap data while peer review R3 includes polymerization defect data (C33, C46-C47). Both support the cooperative mechanism model.

Overlap on polymerization requirement for membrane binding (C33, C46-C47). OpenEval R5 focuses on F130R characterization while peer review R3 emphasizes the broader cooperativity model. Both describe evidence as solid and consistent.

Strong alignment on MD simulation results (C53-C57). OpenEval provides detailed structural findings while peer review emphasizes integration with experimental data. Both support the mechanistic model of MTS-membrane interaction.

Substantial overlap on lipid interaction analysis (C58-C62, C81). OpenEval R8 focuses on contact and energy analysis while peer review R2 groups with broader mechanistic claims (C6). Both describe MD simulations as well-integrated with experimental approaches.

Alignment on mechanistic model (C6). OpenEval R9 synthesizes mutagenesis, binding, and MD data to support the dual hydrophobic-electrostatic mechanism. Peer review R2 includes this with detailed simulation results, describing evidence as solid.

Overlap on PbpC interaction mapping (C69, C71-C72). OpenEval R12 also includes BLI binding data (C70) that peer review addresses in R9. Both support identification of the C1 region as critical for BacA-PbpC interaction.

Alignment on HDX-MS analysis (C73, C82). OpenEval emphasizes conformational changes at polymerization interface while peer review notes this as part of comprehensive interaction site identification. Both describe evidence as consistent.

Overlap on polymerization requirement for PbpC recruitment (C9-C10, C83). OpenEval emphasizes avidity model while peer review groups with broader interaction characterization. Both support the finding that polymerization enhances client binding.

Alignment on independence of BacA localization from PbpC (C74). Both evaluations support this finding as part of characterizing the directional relationship between BacA membrane binding and client recruitment.

Overlap on background claims about BacA-PbpC relationship (C28-C29, C67). OpenEval R11 focuses on new experimental data while peer review R12 groups with broader literature context. Both support the established role of BacA in PbpC localization.

Strong overlap on background literature claims (C1-C3, C13-C25). OpenEval R1 focuses on bactofilin biology context while peer review R12 includes broader background including membrane composition (C77-C78). Both treat these as established knowledge.

Overlap on prior findings establishing knowledge gap (C4, C26-C27). OpenEval emphasizes transmembrane helix prevalence while peer review groups with general background. Both support these as established context for the study.

Partial overlap on single-particle tracking data (C38-C39). OpenEval R4 includes comprehensive membrane binding characterization while peer review R8 specifically notes mobility differences. Both describe evidence as solid.

Alignment on mild phenotypic effects (C70). OpenEval notes C1 dispensability for stalk elongation while peer review observes mild effects of abolished BacA-PbpC interaction. Both findings are consistent and uncontested.

Minimal overlap on F130R structural characterization (C32). OpenEval R5 emphasizes polymerization defects while peer review R11 briefly notes structural validation. Both support the characterization as part of broader analysis.

Minimal overlap on polymerization capability (C31). OpenEval notes Δ2-8 can still polymerize while peer review briefly acknowledges structural characterization. Both treat this as supporting data for functional studies.

Minimal overlap on PbpC as main BacA interactor (C68). OpenEval R11 focuses on deletion studies while peer review R5 emphasizes interaction site mapping. Both support BacA-PbpC interaction characterization.

Overlap on membrane composition background (C77-C78). OpenEval R16 specifically addresses lipid composition justification for simulations while peer review R12 groups with general background. Both treat as established context.
